articles.title: The new chief justice: Who is Rodil Zalameda?
articles.summary: This marks the second appointment of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to the Supreme Court and the first to the position of chief justice.

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 4:29pm
Supreme Court Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda on the sidelines of an Integrated Bar of the Philippines in Roxas City in August 2023.
SC PIO
MANILA, Philippines — A new chief justice has been appointed, filling the highest post in the judiciary as Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo reaches compulsory retirement on November 6.
This marks the second appointment of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to the Supreme Court and the first to the position of chief justice.
On November 5, Presidential Communications Office chief Lino Cayetano announced that Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda had been appointed to the highest post in the judiciary.
He was chosen over two other senior justices appointed by the late President Benigno Aquino III, namely Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda.
Other shortlisted candidates included former President Rodrigo Duterte's detained associates, Associate Justices Japar Dimaampao and Jose Midas Marquez.
What will be Zalameda’s role?

The 1987 Constitution does not mandate any formal role for the chief justice other than serving as an ex-officio chairman of the Judicial and Bar Council and presiding over any impeachment trial of the president.

Despite holding the highest position in the judiciary, his vote carries the same weight as those of the other justices, with only 1 vote out of 15, as he is considered “first among equals” and not superior to the other justices.
He is also required to personally certify every decision rendered by the court.
Who is Zalameda?
Zalameda graduated from Ateneo de Manila University School of Law in 1987. He passed the Bar Examinations in 1988.
According to reports, after passing the bar, Zalameda worked as a clerk at the Makati Regional Trial Court for two years.
He then entered private practice before returning to government service in 1995 as a prosecutor in Mandaluyong. He became assistant city prosecutor in 1997 and city prosecutor in 2002.
RELATED: NCR chief prosecutors endorse Zalameda for chief justice
He served in the position until his appointment to the Court of Appeals on Sept. 5, 2008.
In 2019, Duterte appointed Zalameda as an associate justice of the Supreme Court, replacing Associate Justice Mariano del Castillo, who retired on July 29, 2019.
He was the first Supreme Court appointee to take a decision-writing exam in addition to an interview conducted by the Judicial and Bar Council.
Notable decisions penned by Zalameda
During his stint as an associate justice, Zalameda penned several notable decisions.

Zalameda was the ponente in the Deduro vs. Vinoya decision in 2023, which declared that red-tagging is a threat to life, liberty and security and that individuals being red-tagged can avail themselves of the writ of amparo.

He also penned the June 2026 decision acquitting former First Lady Imelda Marcos. Zalameda acquitted the former first lady of seven counts of graft involving Swiss foundations, reversing a 2018 Sandiganbayan decision.
RELATED: What Supreme Court's Imelda Marcos acquittal means, and what it doesn't

Zalameda also wrote a 2023 ruling stating that a minor above 15 but below 18 may still be criminally liable if the prosecution proves that the child acted with discernment. In this case, Zalameda upheld a homicide conviction.

articles.title: Rappler Talk: Understanding a ‘Wolf World’ with Marc Saxer
articles.summary: Marc Saxer talks to Rappler's Bea Cupin about the profound transformation in the global order. Watch it here at 5 pm, Thursday, November 5.

blocks.text: Marc Saxer talks to Rappler's Bea Cupin about the profound transformation in the global order. Watch it here at 5 pm, Thursday, November 5.

MANILA, Philippines — When Marc Saxer went about writing his latest book, Geopolitical Conflict in the Wolf World, the United States under Donald Trump had just announced “liberation day” tariffs. Before he could submit his final draft, the US and Israel launched an attack on Iran, the consequences of which continue to be felt across the world nearly nine months in.

Saxer, Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Head of Regional Project Indo-Pacific, writes about the profound transformation in the global order, posits the end of Pax Americana, the return of great power rivalry, and conflicts across the world in his latest book.

He also argues for a future through and beyond this chaos — not based on hope or blind optimism but perhaps faith that humanity will always find its way through, and trust that we and our leaders are wise enough to learn from history.
Saxer sits down for Rappler during a quick Manila stop, his last of several cities since mid-2026, to promote his latest book. Catch the interview on at 5 pm on Thursday, November 5. – Rappler.com

articles.title: LIST: VP Sara’s witnesses for Nov. 9–13 hearings
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s lawyers have submitted a witness lineup for the Senate impeachment proceedings.

blocks.text: Headlines
November 5, 2026 | 3:58pm
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte shows a document after posting bail at a court building in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s lawyers have submitted a witness lineup for the Senate impeachment proceedings, in which they plan to call bank officials and city assessors to address the remaining charge against her of alleged unexplained wealth.

In a statement on Thursday, November 5, impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol said the defense filed two manifestations on November 4 asking the court to subpoena 25 individuals for hearings from November 9 to 13.
Presiding officer Sen. Chiz Escudero will act on the requests based on the court’s rules and its standards on relevance and admissibility, Tongol said.
The court also said the trial would go ahead despite a pending Supreme Court challenge to the voter threshold issue.

Through the Office of the Solicitor General, the Senate has asked the High Court to throw out a petition filed by Senators Robin Padilla and Bong Go — both allies of Duterte — and to deny their plea for a restraining order.
First witness declines to appear
The defense’s planned first witness however — Ralph Sarmiento, a former law dean at the University of St. La Salle in Bacolod City — has asked to not be called to the stand.
Sarmiento, who was scheduled to testify Monday on constitutional principles relevant to Article II, said that he was declining “to preserve the independence of my constitutional law scholarship.”
Defense spokesperson Michael Poa said the team respected the decision.

The remaining charge, Article II, accuses Duterte of amassing unexplained wealth, failing to fully declare her and her husband’s assets in her statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN), and retaining business interests barred by the Constitution.
House prosecutors dropped the three other articles — on confidential funds, bribery and grave threats — when they rested their case on October 13.
Here is the defense’s list of intended witnesses for November 9 to 13, according to the impeachment court:

articles.title: Italian chef fired after refusing to put pineapple on pizza
articles.summary: He had told his employer, an Australian restaurant, that pineapple on pizza was "offensive" to Italian culture.

blocks.text: An Italian chef sacked from a Brisbane restaurant had refused to put pineapple on a pizza because it was an "insult to his culture".
Davide Tamburella was fired from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in May, a fortnight after a meeting with management who had a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour.

Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function. At the time, the chef had stated that any direction from management "need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture".
The details came to light after the chef went to Australia's Fair Work Commission claiming he had been unfairly dismissed.

In its ruling released on Tuesday, the commission noted that Tamburella's refusal to put pineapple on the pizzas was because "he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture".
It also noted that it was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years.
He had previously requested his boss to "check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza".
The state of Queensland, where the restaurant is located, is considered Australia's pineapple heartland and produces all of the country's commercially-grown pineapples.
On the Sunshine Coast, visitors regularly stop to take photos next to The Big Pineapple, a heritage-listed 16m-tall fibreglass model of the fruit, which has become a local landmark.
Other concerns were raised about Tamburella using foul language, his communication style and "escalation of frustration in the workplace".
The ruling also detailed an incident at work in April this year where Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand when he struck a metal hand rail.
Tamburella had been hoping the restaurant would sponsor a visa for him that allows skilled workers to be permanent residents.
However after his sacking, the restaurant ended that process, the tribunal heard.
He lost his unfair dismissal claim on the grounds that the application had been filed too late, according to the ruling.
The restaurant's managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was "more to this story than a pizza topping".
The BBC has approached Tamburella for comment.
On the chef's LinkedIn profile, he describes himself as someone who, throughout his career, has focused on "delivering exceptional food" and "improving business performance".
Three months ago he posted a "letter for chefs" with the theme "respecting the ingredients".
The LinkedIn profile states he now works at another Brisbane restaurant. A BBC check has found that pineapple is not on that restaurant's menu.

articles.title: Who is Dean Ralph Sarmiento, tapped by Sara Duterte's camp as witness
articles.summary: Law professor Dean Ralph Sarmiento was listed as Vice President Sara Duterte"s first witness at her impeachment trial. He, however, decided to decline to participate as a witness a day after the…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 3:44pm

Law professor Dean Ralph Sarmiento was listed as Vice President Sara Duterte’s first witness at her impeachment trial. He, however, decided to decline to participate as a witness a day after the announcement was made.
So who is Sarmiento, and why was he called to become a witness for the Vice President?

On his Facebook profile, Sarmiento listed several educational institutions he attended. In 1992, he received his Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science at University of Negros Occidental – Recoletos.

He earned his Juris Doctor degree at the University of St. La Salle (USLS), where he would spend most of his professional career. Sarmiento graduated Magna Cum Laude from USLS and placed 10th in the 1997 Bar Exams, according to publisher Centralbooks, where the law professor has two books.

In 2002, Sarmiento also studied Classical Works and Scholarly Approaches to the U.S. Constitution as a Fulbright Institute fellow at Temple University in the United States, according to his Facebook profile.
Sarmiento would also go on to study Constitutional and Territorial Reforms in Federal Switzerland as a Swiss Institute of Federalism scholar at the University of Fribourg in 2008.
According to Sarmiento’s LinkedIn page, he has over 28 years of experience working as a law professor at the USLS, where he held various positions.

From June 1998 to May 2010, he was the executive director of the school’s Law Center. From 2010 to 2016, he was the university’s College of Law Dean. He took the position once more from August 2023 to January 2026.

By October 2025, he became the USLS’s Vice Chancellor for Administration. While both his LinkedIn and Facebook profiles still list him as presently working as a vice chancellor, Duterte’s defense team labeled him a “former Vice Chancellor for Administration.”
Sarmiento has over 318,000 followers on Facebook.
During Duterte’s trial, Sarmiento has offered his legal opinions on the matter to several news outlets. Many of his views, however, could also be found online.

“We should hold VP Sara Duterte accountable for every peso of public money and every act properly charged against her. But accountability loses its moral force when fairness is sacrificed. Due process is not a favor to the accused. It is what makes accountability credible,” Sarmiento said in a Facebook post on October 14.

“The Constitution does not ask us to choose between accountability and due process. It demands both, and I support both. I support accountability. I also support due process. We should not have to choose between the two. The stronger the accusation, the greater the need for a complete and tested record,” he added.
The post came a day after the House prosecution dropped three out of the four articles of impeachment against Duterte.
Duterte’s defense team decried the dropping of the cases, as it did not give them a chance to defend the Vice President. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Barangay certificates, cedulas not valid for voter registration – Comelec
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Barangay certificates and cedulas will not be accepted as proof of identity for voter registration, Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chair George Erwin Garcia said. The voter…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Barangay certificates and cedulas will not be accepted as proof of identity for voter registration, Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chair George Erwin Garcia said.
The voter registration period will run from Nov. 10 to July 30, 2027, allowing Filipinos to register, transfer their registration or reactivate their voter status.
Garcia reminded the public to use other valid identification documents when applying for voter registration.
“We will no longer accept barangay certification as evidence of a person’s identity in the place where they are registering,” he said in an ambush interview on Thursday, Nov. 5.

Garcia urged applicants to use government-issued identification documents, such as passports, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) clearances, police clearances, the National ID, postal IDs and driver’s licenses.
The commission also accepts library cards, student IDs and senior citizen IDs, provided these bear the applicant’s name, photograph and address.
Meanwhile, the Comelec earlier announced on its Facebook page that it also accepts the electronic Philippine Identification (e-PhilID) when presented through the eGov app.
According to Garcia, the commission had found cases in which barangay officials issued residency certificates to individuals who were not actual residents of their barangays.
“We have found that some individuals used these [documents], which we are investigating and which are now the subject of cases before the Comelec,” he said.
“We found that some barangay officials, in particular, issued barangay certifications to individuals who were not actually residents of their barangays,” he noted.
The commission is targeting at least 3 million additional registered voters before the 2028 national and local elections, bringing the total to 74 million from the current 71 million.
“Currently, we have 71 million registered voters, and our plan is to add 3 million, bringing the total to 74 million voters by 2028,” the poll chief said. /apl

At the 3rd Delhi Defence Dialogue via video teleconference on Wednesday, Teodoro said the Philippines wants to increase the number of BrahMos units it has acquired from India.

"We hope to increase the number of BrahMos units we have, and we have shared also a wish list on the BrahMos to the Indian authorities in order to make it more tailor-fitted for the Philippine environment," he said.
Teodoro cited logistical challenges in operating and transporting the missile system in the Philippines, including the country's less durable roads and bridges and the absence of an active railroad.
He also pointed out the difficulty of transporting military equipment across the country's more than 7,600 islands.
The Philippines became the first foreign country to acquire the BrahMos missile system from India.

Teodoro said the acquisition is a significant demonstration of India's trust and confidence in the Philippines. According to him, Indian authorities had determined that the country would use the capability responsibly and only for defensive purposes consistent with international law.
In August 2025, President Ferdinand ''Bongbong'' Marcos Jr. said the Philippines is in the process of procuring more BrahMos missiles.
In April 2024, the Indian government confirmed that the first batch of BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles was successfully delivered to the Philippines.

Meanwhile, Teodoro identified other potential areas of defense cooperation between the Philippines and Indi including space technology, ground-based air defense systems, multiple-launch rocket systems, and satellite acquisition for the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).
He said Marcos had instructed to pursue an AFP satellite acquisition program with India seen as a potential partner. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: DOTr's Vince Dizon wants review of motorcycle taxi riders cap
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon is looking into reviewing the ceilings on the allowed number of riders on motorcycle-taxi service providers being enforced by the Land Transportation Franchising…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 3:26pm

Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon is looking into reviewing the ceilings on the allowed number of riders on motorcycle-taxi service providers being enforced by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB).
In a chance interview with reporters, Dizon said, in a mix of Filipino and English, "What I want to understand is what is the current supply and demand situation here in Metro Manila."

"How many passengers are there? How many vehicles are available? It is very clear that there is a scarcity. So this regulation on the… maximum number of riders, I think should be reviewed as I believe that this maximum number if no longer applicable," the Transportation chief said.
"So, it will be discussed with the LTFRB," he said, referring to the motorcycle-taxi rider caps.
Dizon made the pronouncement amid the LTFRB's probe into motorcycle-taxi provider Move It, which was reportedly fined for allegedly exceeding its total authorized limit of 17,746 riders by 55,7575.

In a separate statement, the Coalition of Filipino Commuters (CFC) expressed support to Dizon's pronouncement to review the cap on motorcycle taxi riders and to base regulation on actual commuter demand.

"As the Transport Secretary has pointed out, the current limits were set before the pandemic and no longer reflect conditions on the ground, where public transport in Metro Manila remains scarce. For many commuters, motorcycle taxis are no longer just an alternative," CFC said.

"With Metro Manila generating an estimated 16 million trips a day, according to JICA transport studies, limiting the capacity of these services risks further straining an already overstretched system. Caps do not close the underlying shortage of public transport —they shrink service availability, lengthen waiting times, and leave commuters stranded at the curb with nowhere else to turn," the group said.
CFC said it recognizes that "regulation matters," but it should make these services safer and more accountable, not less accessible.
"Any limit on supply should rest on demonstrable public interest, not on figures that no longer match what commuters need," it said. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Fact check: Viral post falsely tags e-trikes at Marcos’ plant visit as gov't vehicles
articles.summary: Viral post mislabels e-trikes at Marcos’ plant visit as new government vehicles.

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 3:19pm
President Bongbong Marcos tries out an electric tricycle during his visit to the Sazgar Philippines Incorporated manufacturing and assembly plant in Biñan City, Laguna, on October 29, 2026.
RTVM / Screenshot
MANILA, Philippines — A viral Facebook reel falsely presents electric tricycles shown during President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s visit to a manufacturing plant as newly acquired government vehicles.

In an October 30 post, Facebook account Trillchaser Motovlog showed a video of Marcos trying out a blue e-tricycle, with a text overlay criticizing the “downgrade” of the supposedly new vehicles of government offices amid the “modern era.”
A viral Facebook reel falsely claims that electric tricycles shown during President Bongbong Marcos’ visit to a manufacturing plant are newly acquired government vehicles.
Screenshot taken Nov. 5, 2026, 2:20 p.m.
The post’s caption also said:
E-TRIKE ???????????? PARANG NAG DOWNGRADE ATAH ANG GOBERNO NGAYON IMBIS NA MAG UPGRADE ????????
Rating: This is false.
Facts
The clip used in the Facebook reel was obtained from Marcos’ visit to the manufacturing and assembly plant of Sazgar Philippines Incorporated (SPI) in Biñan City, Laguna on October 29.
Marcos was seen trying out one of SPI’s e-tricycle models during the plant’s inauguration. SPI is a subsidiary of Pakistan-based Sazgar Engineering Works Limited.
There were no mentions of acquisition or procurement of the e-tricycles as government vehicles in Marcos’ speech during the visit.
Instead, he only highlighted how the investment reflects what can be achieved when the government and private sector work together.
Marcos said the plant qualified under the Strategic Investment Priority Plan as it “adds real value locally.”
“That is the kind of investment that we want. Not just companies that sell to Filipinos, but companies that make things with Filipinos,” he said.
The president also noted how the Philippines is “keen” on transitioning towards electric vehicles.
“In fact, we have directed all government agencies to prioritize the purchase of EVs or consider EVs when renting motor vehicles,” he said.
However, Marcos was referring to a general government directive on electric vehicles. He did not say that the e-tricycles shown during his visit had been acquired for government use.

On the same day, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro mentioned the attendance of Marcos at the inauguration of SPI, highlighting the plant’s opening as an important step toward a stronger infrastructure industry and cleaner transportation in the country.

“Kaninang umaga, pinangunahan ni Pangulong Marcos Jr. ang pagpapasinaya sa manufacturing at assembly plant ng Sazgar Philippines Inc. sa Laguna. Malinaw ang mensahe ng pangulo na ang pagbubukas ng planta ay isang mahalagang hakbang tungo sa mas matatag na infrastructure industry at mas malinis na transportasyon sa bansa,” she said.
Castro likewise did not announce any government acquisition of the e-tricycles.
Why we fact-checked this
The post comes amid other viral claims involving government vehicles that have drawn criticism against the administration.

In October, several high-engagement posts falsely claimed that fire trikes shown in different localities cost P10 million each, drawing criticism on social media against Marcos and Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla.
As of November 5, the reel has garnered more than 7,000 views, 400 reactions and 100 comments.

articles.title: Ministers to target ‘wild west’ of e-bikes blocking pavements
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Consultation led by Department for Transport will consider parking standards, fleet sizes and insurance requirements

Ministers are seeking to end the “wild west” of parked e-bikes…

blocks.text: Ministers are seeking to end the “wild west” of parked e-bikes blocking pavements, as they attempt to crack down on antisocial behaviour such as cyclists jumping red lights.

The consultation, led by the Department for Transport, will aim to establish national standards on issues including parking, ending the current patchwork of agreements between individual bike companies and councils.

While some areas enforce rules that mean shared bikes – such as those operated by Lime, Forest and Voi – can only be left in designated parking bays, elsewhere the rules are looser, prompting complaints about bikes blocking pavements, particularly for wheelchair users, people with pushchairs and those with impaired vision.
It will also look at antisocial and illegal riding, for example, people jumping lights or the use of bikes by those who are underage or drunk.

The plans will also examine guidelines for fleet sizes to ensure certain areas are not overcrowded and possible requirements for operators to have insurance, so someone hit by a rider on a hired e-bike can claim compensation.

Another part of the consultation will look at whether councils and mayors should be given powers over the fees charged to rent bikes, and whether companies should share data to improve enforcement and transport planning.

Since arriving in the UK in 2018, shared e-bike systems, of which Lime is by some way the biggest, have expanded rapidly, especially in London. More than 2.6 million Britons used an e-bike share scheme in the year to September 2025, according to one estimate.

There is evidence that shared e-bikes are used by a broader demographic range of riders than traditional bikes, in part because of the electric assistance, but also because they do not require somewhere secure to park.

The DfT argues that the bikes are growing in importance for urban transport, but that the lack of any central oversight has created difficulties, noting that the companies themselves have called for more regulation.

The proposed changes would be “a small but important everyday fix to make our streets safer”, Andy Burnham said. The prime minister added: “E-bikes can make getting around that bit easier, but when they block pavements or are used irresponsibly they can be a real frustration.
“I want to sort that by giving communities more control over where they are parked and making sure companies and riders play by the rules.”

Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, said: “Shared e-bike schemes have revolutionised the way people travel around our towns and cities. They are easy to use, get us active and help reduce emissions, but we need to make sure they work with the communities where they operate.
“That’s why we are taking decisive action to give local leaders the power to stop nuisance parking, tackle antisocial behaviour and make journeys safer.”

There are parallel efforts in London under which the DfT would devolve power to the mayor, Sadiq Khan, and Transport for London to unify e-bike regulations, which are currently the responsibility of individual boroughs and vary significantly.

Khan said: “The ‘wild west’ approach to dockless e-bikes cannot continue. While these services are helping thousands more Londoners to cycle, their rapid growth has also brought challenges around safety, inconsiderate parking and the lack of data needed to properly manage them.

“I’ve been calling for powers to better manage dockless e-bike schemes since 2017, when the first schemes arrived in London, so I welcome the government’s plans to give cities the powers they need to do this.”

articles.title: A Democratic-controlled Congress will likely try to constrain Trump’s foreign adventures
articles.summary:
But the president still has veto power, which he can wield to dictate policy over tariffs, the war in Iran or aid for Ukraine

In a rare occurrence, a US election may have actually been…

blocks.text: In a rare occurrence, a US election may have actually been decided by foreign policy. Donald Trump’s war in Iran and international tariffs are seen as playing a key role in the inflationary pressures that drove so many Americans to vote against his party on Tuesday in what has been described as a “generational wipeout” for the Republicans.

And in the coming months, the president is going to face severe headwinds on those policies as Democrats storm back into control of Congress, threatening investigations of some of his top envoys and Pentagon contractors, big fights over budgets linked to the Iran war, and greater scrutiny of US relationships with allies such as Israel.

While Democrats plot their strategy, the civil war within the Republican party has already begun. JD Vance was early out of the gate, announcing in a postmortem on X that the Republicans’ shellacking was directly linked to Trump’s decision to strike Iran. “The reason we lost is the war,” he said. “The president himself said so last night.” Soon Donald Trump Jr was chiming in: “Every word of this is 💯💯💯.”

Trump Sr partly confirmed the vice-president’s analysis, admitting that the war had pushed gasoline prices up. But he added that he believed the Iran war was worth it, and that “we had to do it, we continue to do it”.

“Long term, it’s the only answer,” he said. “You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.” Seeing little left to lose, he may resume strikes in the upcoming months, seeking to secure his legacy with fewer concerns about voter backlash with the midterms already passed.

Democrats will hold a majority in both houses of Congress, but won’t be able to override a presidential veto to force legislation into law. So the likely battles in the coming months will be focused on finding leverage to constrain the White House – most clearly through Congress’s control of the budget.

“The Democrats taking control of both houses gives them unprecedented leverage – especially using the budget,” said Ryan Crocker, a former career diplomat and diplomatic fellow at the Middle East Institute, a thinktank. “We have seen the [Pentagon] request to dramatically increase funding to support the war with Iran come into substantial criticism from Democrats, and I think that will be the first battleground.”

Democrats will have an early opportunity to pressure the Trump administration during the lame duck session of Congress in December, when funding for the government through a continuing resolution is set to expire. They could also hold hostage the passage of the National Defense Authorization Act, demanding concessions on Iran or limits on Trump’s authority in order to pass the Senate version of the bill that would authorise about $1.15tn in national defense spending for 2027.

One progressive foreign policy thinktank suggested inserting language into the continuing resolution that would prevent Trump from using the money authorised by Congress to fund the war in Iran, as well as in Yemen, Lebanon and Gaza. But shutting down the government could be a “two-edged sword”, said Crocker, and Democrats will have to be careful not to overplay their hand.

“American voters were pretty angry in this midterm election – they were voting against President Trump and his actions and policies as much as they were voting for [Democrats] – and that means that Democrats will have to be careful how they use this power.”

Democrats had little success in 2019 restraining Trump from unpopular foreign policy decisions like an abrupt withdrawal from Syria that abandoned Kurdish allies or to end his support for the Saudi war in Yemen. When Congress managed to pass a bipartisan resolution that invoked the War Powers Act to end US support for Saudi Arabia in the deadly war, Trump simply vetoed it.
after newsletter promotion

Even with control of both houses of Congress, it will remain difficult for Democrats to constrain Trump’s power to dictate foreign policy over tariffs, the war in Iran or aid for Ukraine such as intelligence sharing, deliveries of desperately needed Patriot interceptors or access to the Starlink satellite internet service.

“It is worth watching how and where the new Congress chooses to convert its investigative energies into real policy constraints on the executive branch,” wrote Jennifer Hendrixson White, a visiting scholar in the American Statecraft Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. “Congressional investigations into the Iran war or defense contracts with Trump-linked firms could pressure or embarrass the president, but it is less clear whether a Democratic-controlled House or Senate would be able to convert those investigations into meaningful actions.”

Still, the elections have upended the status quo for foreign policy in both parties, and Trump will increasingly face pressure from his own allies to end the war in Iran. Vance, in his public statement about the elections, prescribed his cure for what is ailing the Republican party: “1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel.”

That also marks a dangerous moment for Israel, wrote Amit Segal, a political analyst close to the Netanyahu administration, which “now faces its biggest challenge in Washington since at least the 1975 ‘reassessment’, when Ford and Kissinger froze arms deals to pressure Jerusalem,” he wrote.

Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who will be the first sitting Muslim senator next year, illustrated how far US policy has shifted in this election as he praised Trump’s decision to end military aid to Israel at the end of this year. “I think the president is actually right on this policy,” he said. “I’d also like to see us stop selling weaponry that gets used to do the worst things, including genocide and apartheid, to Israel.”

articles.title: Warming UK seas could ‘fundamentally reshape marine ecosystems’ – report
articles.summary:
Four-year study warns destabilised marine food webs could jeopardise food security by 2050

Warming seas around the UK and the wider north-east Atlantic could destabilise marine food webs,…

blocks.text: Warming seas around the UK and the wider north-east Atlantic could destabilise marine food webs, weaken ocean health and jeopardise food security by 2050, according to a four-year study.

Scientists who projected the impact of climate breakdown on four key groups of marine life crucial to maintaining ocean ecosystems in the region said their results challenged assumptions that in middle latitudes, such as the UK, marine biodiversity was likely to increase across the board.
Instead, their projections highlight a predator-prey imbalance that could “fundamentally reshape marine ecosystems” in unforeseen ways, they said.
The seas around the British isles, particularly the southern North Sea, have been identified as “marine climate hotspots”, one of 20 globally to have warmed the fastest over 50 years.

The new predictions, under a scenario of 3C (5.4F) of warming by 2100, found that while fish and seabed invertebrates may become more diverse by mid-century, key plankton groups lower in the food chain were likely to decline. This imbalance, the authors of the report said, could disrupt marine food webs and weaken the health and resilience of ocean ecosystems.

“What surprised us is that warming doesn’t increase or decrease biodiversity across the board,” said Elena Couce, a marine ecologist at the Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science (Cefas), a British government agency, and co-lead author of the study.

“While some groups higher up the food chain, like fish, may gain species in parts of the north-east Atlantic, key plankton groups that underpin marine ecosystems are projected to lose species,” she said.

The research, led by Cefas and published in Science Advances, involved an international team of researchers from the University of East Anglia, the Marine Biological Association, UiT the Arctic University of Norway, the Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research and the Technical University of Denmark.

blocks.caption: Pleurobrachia, a zooplankton genus known as the sea gooseberry. Crucial zooplankton could decline by about 7% by mid-century, the study found. Photograph: Hannah Lloyd-Hartley/Cefas

blocks.text: “When things get hotter, all the species from the equator are going to move north and south,” Cource said. “The UK is in the middle latitudes. So we expected diversity to go up, because you get species from the south that are more diverse than the species you lose to the north.”

Previous Cefas research looking at key fish species suggested warming in north-western European waters would result in climate “winners”, such as anchovies, seabass and sardines. Such conditions, however, are less suitable for climate “losers”, including Atlantic cod, haddock and coley.

The current study, focusing on ecosystems in UK waters and the wider north-east Atlantic including Ireland and France, found that by mid-century, fish and seabed invertebrate diversity could increase by about 12%, whereas phytoplankton and zooplankton diversity could decline by about 3% and 7%, respectively by 2050.

“If predator diversity rises while prey diversity falls, that has the potential to disrupt the food chain,” said Lily Greig, a marine ecologist at Cefas who also co-led the study. “Our results show that climate change could reshuffle marine biodiversity unevenly across the food web, and that gains in some groups do not necessarily mean the ecosystem as a whole is becoming more resilient.”

By identifying where biodiversity was changing fastest and which parts of the ecosystem were most at risk, the study could provide an “early warning system” of potential ecosystem change, the researchers said. The work has already been submitted to the government’s review of marine protected areas, which is looking at fishery management measures.

“Policymakers have a mandate to try to preserve or even increase biodiversity,” said Couce. “What we are trying to tell them is climate change is already changing biodiversity, and you need to take that into account before you can make other management plans.”

The scientists used multiple long-term datasets and advanced machine-learning techniques to determine the relationship between biodiversity and environmental change, which enabled them to predict climate-driven biodiversity change until 2100.

articles.title: Speaker Dy backs calls for greater budget transparency
articles.summary: Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III on Thursday said that Dy said the House of Representatives is open to disclosing supporting documents for government projects and make budget deliberations more…

blocks.text: 'WALANG DAPAT ITAGO'
Published November 5, 2026 2:56pm

Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III on Thursday said that Dy said the House of Representatives is open to disclosing supporting documents for government projects and make budget deliberations more accessible to the public.
“Walang dapat itago kung walang ginagawang mali. At walang dapat katakutan kung ang layunin ay maglingkod nang tapat,” Dy said.
(There is nothing to hide if nothing wrong is being done. And there is nothing to fear if the intention is to serve honestly.)
“Ang badyet ay pera ng taumbayan. Karapatan nilang malaman kung paano ito ginagastos,” he added.
(The budget is the people's money. It is their right to know how it is being spent.)

The People’s Budget Coalition has flagged P170 billion increase in budget for multi-purpose buildings and local road projects. It also flagged eight farm to market roads with locations mapped in seas.
The Department of Agriculture has since clarified that the eight farm to market locations with wrong coordinates were a typographical error on its part.
Dy, meanwhile, said that amendments introduced by lawmakers in the P7.2 trillion proposed budget should not be presumed "anomalous."

“Hindi lahat ng pagbabagong ginagawa ng Kongreso sa badyet ay mali. Tungkulin ng mga kongresista na ipaglaban ang pangangailangan ng kanilang mga distrito. Ang mahalaga, maayos ang proyekto, kumpleto ang dokumento at may tunay na pakinabang sa tao,” Dy said.

(Legitimate congressional amendments should not automatically be associated with corruption. What is important here is that the projects are backed up with documents and would be of service to the community.)
The Speaker also expressed support for reforms that would make government assistance more accessible based on people’s needs rather than political connections.

“The House is prepared to work with the Senate, executive agencies and civil society organizations to ensure that public funds address urgent national concerns, including food security, healthcare, education, employment, infrastructure and preparations for El Niño,” he added.
The House has already approved the proposed P7.2 trillion budget on third and final reading.
The Senate is still deliberating on the proposed 2027 national budget.

articles.title: SSS partners with DICT to integrate digital ID into eGov app
articles.summary: The Social Security System (SSS) has partnered with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) to integrate the MySSS Card's digital ID feature and select member services into…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 2:51pm

The Social Security System (SSS) has partnered with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) to integrate the MySSS Card's digital ID feature and select member services into the eGovPH app.
The partnership was forged through a data-sharing agreement signed on October 21, 2026, in Quezon City by DICT Secretary Robert Joseph de Claro and SSS President and CEO Victor Alfonso Limlingan.
The partnership came shortly after de Claro's appointment as DICT Secretary, following his tenure as SSS chief.

"This partnership marks a major step in making SSS services more accessible and convenient for our members. By integrating the digital MySSS Card and key services into the eGovPH superapp, we are bringing social security closer to every Filipino—right at their fingertips," said Limlingan.
Once integrated, the SSS said its members will be able to access the front-facing digital representation of their MySSS Card as one of the IDs available through the eGovPH superapp.
Members will also be able to view their contribution history, total number of contributions, latest membership type, and most recent employer information.

"Our members should not have to visit multiple offices or use multiple applications just to access basic services. Through eGovPH superapp, we are making it easier for Filipinos to check their contributions, verify their membership status, and access their MySSS Card—all in one place," said Limlingan.

articles.summary: Phase 4 of the Malampaya Project reached its first gas milestone, marking the official connection of two new wells near Palawan to the Luzon grid.

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 2:49pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., together with Prime Infra Chairman Enrique Razon, leads the ceremonial push-button activation of the first gas from the Malampaya Phase 4 (MP4) Project at the Malampaya Onshore Gas Plant in Barangay Tabangao Ambulong, Batangas City, on Nov. 5, 2026.
Noel Pabalate and Yummie Dingding via The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — The Malampaya East-1 and Camago-3 wells, discovered earlier this year, have completed their first delivery of natural gas to the Malampaya gas transmission infrastructure in Batangas, officially connecting the wells to power plants serving the Luzon grid.

The wells, located offshore Palawan, add 222 billion cubic feet of recoverable natural gas reserves to the field. These reserves are capable of powering 13.11 million Filipino households and producing around 31.46 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity.

The discovery of these wells, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said, may lead to more competitive power rates because of reduced reliance on imported energy resources. Malampaya gas costs P4.80 per kilowatt-hour, almost half the price of imported liquefied natural gas.

More than half of the country's energy resources come from abroad, leaving the sector susceptible to supply disruptions linked to geopolitical tensions. The Department of Energy has been urged to penalize erring power firms amid high electricity prices, as well as recurring grid alerts in the Visayas and Mindanao.

Housing, water, electricity and gas costs pushed inflation in October to 7.8%, the highest rate seen in almost four years. The index, which accelerated to 9.3% from 8.4% in September, also drove up transport costs. Prices have continued to soar due to conflict in the Middle East, though eased export restrictions in East and Southeast Asian markets have dampened price hikes.
A state of national energy emergency was declared on March 24 and will last for one year, unless extended or lifted by the president.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: No court order for GMA Network’s shutdown over libel complaint
articles.summary: A complaint filed with prosecutors was falsely presented as a court ruling ordering the network’s closure

blocks.text: Claim: GMA Network will be shut down due to libel and cyber libel complaints filed by Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte.

Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube video posted on October 24 by the channel Pinas News Insider carries the title, “WALA NA! FINISH NA! BYE BYE GMA 7, ISASARA NA; HATOL KORTE KOMPIRMAD0NG ANTI VP SARA; DAWIT BBM, NBI”
(It’s over! Finished! Bye-bye GMA 7, to be shut down, court ruling confirmed, anti-VP Sara, BBM, NBI implicated.)
The thumbnail then asks with a superimposed text, “GMA sarado na?! Karma ang inabot, hatol sa korte?!” (Is GMA closed already?! Did karma catch up with it? A court ruling?!)
The video had 78,000 views and 4,200 likes as of writing.
The facts: No court ruling, government order, or credible report indicated that GMA Network is closing. The case involves a complaint, not a court verdict.

Duterte personally filed a cyber libel complaint on October 23 with Davao City’s Office of the City Prosecutor over a September 25 episode of GMA’s news program 24 Oras, which aired pre-recorded interviews with dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag. Gracioso alleged that he delivered suitcases of cash to the Duterte family (READ: The Gracioso affidavit: Ex-cop claims he delivered millions to Sara Duterte).

Duterte named Matibag, Gracioso, GMA chairman Felipe Gozon, president and chief executive Gilberto Duavit Jr., and anchors, including Mel Tiangco and Vicky Morales, as respondents. He is seeking P10 million in moral damages and another P10 million in exemplary damages.
Vice President Sara Duterte denied Gracioso’s allegations and said he is purely driven by money.

Filing a complaint does not automatically lead to criminal charges or affect GMA Network’s operations. Under the Rules of Criminal Procedure, the prosecutor must first conduct a preliminary investigation and determine whether probable cause exists to bring the case to court. Only then can it file formal charges.
GMA Network has not announced any closure. As of October 23, the network said it had yet to receive a copy of the complaint and would review the matter.

Libel complaint: Press groups and lawmakers have criticized the complaint. The National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) GMA Chapter condemned the complaint on October 23, saying the report had undergone “standard, multilayered editorial and legal verification.”

Mamamayang Liberal (ML) Representative Leila de Lima said suing journalists over reports on corruption allegations sends a chilling message to other media practitioners. Duterte, meanwhile, said he was merely defending his family.

On October 26, Matibag sought to remove the Davao City prosecutor handling the complaint and move its venue to the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) national prosecution service. The NBI investigation into Gracioso’s allegations is ongoing. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

blocks.text: Here are the latest headlines from across Germany on Thursday, November 5:
November 5, 2026
Overall deportations down, but returns to Turkey on the rise

The number of people deported from Germany decreased by nearly 19% from January to September 2026 compared to the previous year, the Interior Ministry announced following a request from the Left Party.
Some 14,324 people were deported in the first nine months of this year, down from 17,651 in 2025. Turkey was the most common destination, followed by Georgia and Algeria.
The numbers reveal that deportations to Syria remain difficult due to the political situation there, even for convicted criminals. Six people have been returned there since the beginning of 2026.
Deportations to Turkey, however, appeared to buck the trend, as 2,025 people have been sent there.

According to the Interior Ministry, the number of foreign nationals leaving the country voluntarily has also slightly increased. Some 14,140 people have received assistance to return to their countries of origin, compared to 12,263 the year before.

articles.title: Romualdez is jailed, but can he keep staff in his cell?
articles.summary: 'Actually I approved it because we cannot supply 24/7 [staff] who will assist [Romualdez]…His mental state is not yet stable,' says the jail warden

blocks.text: ROMUALDEZ. File photo of former speaker Martin Romualdez.
Aaron Favila/AP/Sandiganbayan pool
'Actually I approved it because we cannot supply 24/7 [staff] who will assist [Romualdez]…His mental state is not yet stable,' says the jail warden
There were reports that circulated, claiming that former speaker Martin Romualdez is allowed to go in and out of the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas where he is detained.
Romualdez, cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., has been under arrest since September 7, when the Office of the Ombudsman charged him with a P7.4-billion plunder case.
What’s the real score? Is the once powerful lawmaker enjoying special treatment?

“News…have been circulating online. So to find out the truth of that matter, we have called this hearing,” said Sandiganbayan 3rd Division chairperson Associate Justice Karl Miranda, whose chamber handles the plunder case.

Miranda called on two Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) officials — Jail Superintendent Maria Lourdes Pacion (warden) and Jail Chief Inspector Henry Fabro (jail doctor) — to clarify reports.

“I categorically deny the information and we did not…. Since the commitment of Congressman Martin Romualdez…. He just stayed in the room…. He did not go out riding an ambulance or any other vehicle,” Pacion told the court during the hearing on Thursday, November 5.
Pacion said Romualdez is currently detained inside a dormitory cell. He spent the first three weeks in Payatas jail inside the infirmary due to hypertension.
“There is an embedded air condition in the infirmary…I think so that the patient will feel comfortable,” the jail warden said when asked if there is air-conditioning inside the infirmary.

The jail warden said Romualdez has no personal security inside the jail, but he has personal staff who looks after him. Pacion said his staff has been staying inside the jail since Romualdez was detained on September 14, and attends to the congressman’s personal needs.
Is this even allowed by BJMP rules? Detainees’ relatives or lawyers normally have to schedule visits when needed.

Pacion said: “Actually I approved it because we cannot supply 24/7 [staff] who will assist [Romualdez]… His mental state is not yet stable…. We cannot hire any more persons to put for the personal needs of [the] congressman.”
“It’s actually human considerations…. It’s a case to case basis. It’s the prerogative of the warden, what’s needed for a certain person deprived of liberty (PDL),” she added.
Pacion further defended her decision and said that there had been a case in the past when she allowed a relative of a PDL to stay within the jail area because the PDL needed special care at the time.
“Because BJMP has no [program] tending to special care,” the jail warden said, “I allowed the relative to stay in the area.”

blocks.caption: How Martin Romualdez avoided jail by going to hospital

blocks.text: On Thursday, media personality Ramon Tulfo posted a statement on Facebook, retracting his claim that Romualdez is allowed to go in and out of his detention cell in Payatas.

“I was fed the wrong report that former speaker Martin Romualdez could go in and out of jail. Complete with all the details like riding in an ambulance and the brownouts taking place so he would not be seen going out and coming back in,” said Tulfo.
“No such” thing happened when the facts started coming in yesterday. It was fiction. I goofed. No excuses,” he added.
Romualdez’s lawyer, Ade Fajardo, confirmed to reporters that they have a cease and desist letter against Tulfo.

“The allegations are not harmless pieces of gossip. They impute serious misconduct and extraordinary privileges within a detention facility, and cast aspersions upon the integrity of the officials and personnel tasked with administering our Client’s detention,” said the letter.

During the Thursday hearing, Pacion reiterated that their jail has strict security protocols. Apart from closed circuit televisions (CCTV), security personnel also check all vehicles — including ambulances — that go in and out of the compound.
“They [staff] inspect going out and going in [vehicles]…. Including vehicles of personnel and visitors,” the jail warden said.
The hearing will continue on Monday.

In the meantime, the court ordered BJMP officials to review all CCTV footage from the time Romualdez entered the facility, up to November 4. Pacion and other officials are also required to submit a notarized report detailing Romualdez’s whereabouts based on the recordings.
The officials are also ordered to submit the following, among others:

items: Maintenance records of CCTVs
CCTV access logs
Records of any power interruption in Payatas jail
Vehicle entry and exit logbooks
Identities of the persons allowed to assist Romualdez inside the facility
Records of ambulance use

articles.title: Navy probes alleged reservist over posts on San Andres youth riot
articles.summary: The Philippine Navy will look into online posts made by one of its alleged "reservists" on the recent street brawls at Manila’s San Andres district, warning that he could be dishonorably…

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 2:12pm
Philippine Navy

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Navy will look into online posts made by one of its alleged "reservists" on the recent street brawls at Manila’s San Andres district, warning that he could be dishonorably discharged if he is found to have violated military rules.

Navy spokesperson Capt. Marissa Martinez said in a statement that an “appropriate investigation” would be conducted to establish the accountability of a certain Aristotle Quitana, whom the Navy described as “reportedly” a member of its Reserve Force.
If the probe confirms a violation of military rules and regulations, Quitana “may face appropriate sanctions, including dishonorable discharge from the Reserve Force,” Martinez said.

“The Philippine Navy does not tolerate any remarks that incite violence or show disregard for human life, as these are contrary to the standards of discipline and core values expected of all Navy personnel, including members of the Reserve Force,” she added.
The Navy has not formally confirmed his reservist status.

Police have identified 14 minors involved in the disturbance that broke out early Tuesday along Diamante Street in Barangay 797, after the local police precinct received reports of a group of boys causing trouble.
Street fights have repeatedly broken out among youth groups in Manila where minors have been seen throwing bottles and wielding metal rods at each other.
Under the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act, children aged 15 and below are exempt from criminal liability, while those above 15 but below 18 can be held liable only if they acted with discernment.

Martinez said the Navy “remains committed to upholding the highest standards of discipline, accountability, and professionalism” among both regular and reserve personnel. The Navy did not give a timeline for the investigation.

articles.title: Norman conquest castle and Dickens chalet among sites added to heritage at risk register
articles.summary:
William the Conquerer-built Hastings Castle and Swiss-style writing retreat in Kent two of nearly 200 additions to list

A castle built by William the Conquerer, a Swiss-style chalet where…

blocks.text: A castle built by William the Conquerer, a Swiss-style chalet where Charles Dickens wrote and a swathe of fire-blasted moorland are among sites that have been added to Historic England’s heritage at risk register.

Almost 200 historic places have been added to the already extensive list, including Hastings Castle in East Sussex, Dickens’ wooden writing retreat in Kent and Fylingdales Moor in North Yorkshire, which was devastated by a wildfire in the summer.
Some of the stress on the sites is being put down to the climate emergency, with hotter summers and stormier winters placing some of England’s most treasured places in greater peril.

blocks.caption: Charles Dickens’ writing chalet in Rochester. Photograph: Historic England

blocks.text: Historic England also highlighted more cheerful stories, with sites ranging from a historic Cornish fishing harbour to a rustic West Country hut regarded as the birthplace of vaccinations being removed from the list.

Emma Squire, the joint chief executive of Historic England, said the 197 additions were diverse, and she accepted some people would be surprised that such high-profile sites could be in danger. “It highlights that even places regarded as very special can sometimes be at risk of decay or loss,” she said.

Hastings Castle was one of the fortifications commissioned by William the Conqueror after the Norman invasion of 1066 to secure his position along the English south coast. Historic England said the exposed setting and coastal erosion had long shaped the ruins, but recently sections had become vulnerable because of extreme weather events.
Squire said: “More extreme weather events and coastal erosion are definitely themes. Water ingress and subsidence feature more than they have done in the past because of changing weather patterns.”

Dickens’ writing chalet in Rochester has been added to the register because it is judged to have become fragile and in need of repair. The wooden two-storey building originally stood in Dickens’ garden at Gads Hill Place in Higham, Kent, and served as a getaway where he could work undistracted.
He is thought to have positioned mirrors to help him rehearse for his public performances and develop new characters. The chalet was moved to its present position in Rochester in the 1960s.

blocks.caption: Wildfire damage at Fylingdales Moor.  Photograph: Historic England

blocks.text: The Fylingdales Moor wildfire in 2025 caused damage to about 25 sq km of moorland and forest, according to North Yorkshire fire and rescue service.

Historic England said it affected thousands of people living and working in the area as well as having a major impact on the natural environment. It has been working with the North York Moors National Park Authority using drones to help assess the damage.

Also added to the list is Hall’s Croft in Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, the historic home of William Shakespeare’s daughter. Funding is needed to save the exterior of the 17th-century timber-framed building, including repairing damage caused when it was hit by a vehicle.

blocks.caption: Hall’s Croft in Statford-upon-Avon. Photograph: Steven Baker/Historic England

blocks.text: The 18th-century Bidston windmill in Wirral, Merseyside, which has spectacular views of Liverpool and the Welsh mountains, has also been added. A friends group keeps it open but urgent repairs are needed.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Bidston windmill, Wirral. Photograph: Historic England

blocks.text: Historic England said 85 sites had been “saved” and removed from the register, including Newlyn harbour, one of Cornwall’s most important fishing ports. Local specialists have restored its granite structures and 19th-century wrought iron railings.

blocks.caption: The old harbour pier and walls at Newlyn, Cornwall.  Photograph: Steven Baker/Historic England

blocks.text: In Haringey, north London, 810 Tottenham High Road, a Georgian terrace house, has been saved from dereliction by Tottenham Hotspur FC, with support from the National Lottery Heritage Fund, and is now a creative hub with artists’ studios, galleries and a cafe.

blocks.caption: 810 Tottenham High Road. Photograph: Historic England

blocks.text: Edward Jenner’s hut in Berkeley, Gloucestershire, a rustic summerhouse described as the site of the world’s first vaccination clinic, has also been saved.

blocks.caption: The thatched hut in Berkeley, Gloucestershire.  Photograph: Historic England

blocks.text: Historic England said it spent more than £12m on grants for support and repairs to 135 sites on the heritage at risk register during 2025-26.
There are still almost 5,000 sites on the list, including 1,500 secular buildings, 1,000 places of worship, three battlefields and four wrecks.

The heritage minister, Fiona Twycross, said: “This year’s register is an important reminder of the pressures facing our historic environment, from ageing buildings and structural deterioration to the impacts of extreme weather.”

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has named Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda as the new Supreme Court (SC) chief justice.
He will be replacing Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo who will retire on November 6.
Zalameda was appointed as SC associate justice by then President Rodrigo Duterte on August 6, 2019.

articles.title: US midterm elections 2026 live: Democrats eye historic upset in Mississippi Senate race as Republican blame game begins
articles.summary: Democrat Scott Colom is leading Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in the southern state; JD Vance pointed to the war in Iran as the ‘obvious’ culprit for Republicans’ loss

blocks.text: Mississippi count continues with Democratic candidate ahead by a razor-thin margin
Welcome to our continuing coverage of the 2026 midterms where almost 24 hours after Democrats secured their historic sweep of the US Congress, two Senate seats remain in play.

Counting in Alaska is expected to continue into Thursday, while in deep red Mississippi, Democrats could be close to pulling off another almighty upset. Currently, Democrat Scott Colom is leading his Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by just 1,138 votes with almost 96% of the vote counted.
In the last few hours, votes for Colom have been outpacing those for his Republican opponent, although new batches of votes have not been reported for several hours now.
Although a race this close would automatically trigger a recount in some states, Mississippi has no law on the books for initiating a recount.

blocks.caption: Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom on Wednesday.  Photograph: Sue Dorfman/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Democrats haven’t won a US Senate seat in Mississippi since 1982, and Donald Trump carried the state by 22 points in 2024. It’s been much longer – not since 1875 – that the state elected a Black person to that office.

Colom is a seventh-generation Mississippian, whose father was a Republican who campaigned for Ronald Reagan and was friends with Thad Cochran, a longtime state politician. In 2015, he unseated a nearly 30-year incumbent when he was elected the first Black district attorney for the 16th circuit. As district attorney, he had a 94% success rate for convictions.
Meanwhile, after Democrats secured their historic wins in last night’s midterm elections, Republicans are beginning the blame game:

items: Donald Trump claimed Republicans fared poorly because he was not on the ballot – after repeatedly urging voters to pretend he was on the ballot.
JD Vance pointed to Trump’s ongoing war in Iran as the “obvious” culprit for the loss.

Pete Hegseth’s role leading the unpopular war could lead to him taking the fall – despite Trump publicly backing him. Republicans including Trump foe Thomas Massie have criticized the defense secretary.

Ron DeSantis, Florida’s governor, said the “close to an extinction-level event for Republicans” was caused in part by his party failing to target their ad spending on issues that would motivate voters.

blocks.text: According to exit polls from the Associated Press, voters said the cost of living and government corruption were their two top issues. But how will Trump cope with this new political reality?
The Guardian’s David Smith explores that – and whether these elections mark the beginning of the end for Trump – this analysis piece here:
Key events

items: 19m agoHow papers across the world reacted to Trump's midterm loss
32m agoMississippi count continues with Democratic candidate ahead by a razor-thin margin

blocks.text: Continued from the last post:

Across the US, editors worked into the night on Tuesday to get out late editions of their papers. In Chicago, the Sun Times captured newly elected Senator Juliana Stratton as she celebrated her party’s victory, under the headline “Dem-olition”.

blocks.caption: Photograph: Guardian

blocks.text: A slew of historic wins were recorded throughout the night, including the election of the first Muslim senator, the first openly gay senator and the first black female governor in the US.

Keisha Lance Bottom’s win was described as “historic” by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution – an online publication which produces a daily front page. The paper notes that the governor-elect has shattered “racial and gender glass ceilings” on a day the US elected “four Black governors”.

blocks.caption: Photograph: Guardian

blocks.text: Highlighting the end of the Republican party’s “stranglehold on Texas politics”, the Dallas Morning News captured two of the night’s biggest wins under the headline “Wave of change”.
Senator-elect James Talarico and Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa shared the front page, after a night that saw the Democrats sweep to victory in deep red Texas.

blocks.caption: Photograph: Guardian

blocks.text: With the results showing hispanic voters swinging away from Trump, California’s Spanish-language daily La Opinión produced one of the more memorable front pages.
Above a picture of a battered Maga hat, the paper’s headline simply reads “National punishment”.

blocks.text: How papers across the world reacted to Trump's midterm loss

The results of America’s historic midterm elections reverberated around the world on Wednesday, with front pages reflecting on a night that saw Donald Trump dealt a punishing blow by the US electorate.

“Trumped” was the Guardian’s headline on Thursday’s edition, with reporter Ed Pilkington noting that, with the president’s party stripped of control of Congress, the country was waking up to a “radically altered political landscape”.

blocks.caption: Photograph: Guardian

blocks.text: A late edition of the New York Post captured the scale of Trump’s defeat on Wednesday. Riffing on Hokusai’s Great Wave artwork, the paper notes it was a “historic romp for Democrats”, under the headline “Blue Tsunami”.

blocks.caption: Photograph: Guardian

blocks.text: The English-language Tehran Times, which is closely aligned with the government, said in its headline: “US hegemony crumbling; Iran will never surrender”.
With a selection of midterms stories across the front page, the paper quotes senior figures under a subhead that reads “Iranian officials link Republican election defeat to US war against Iran”.

blocks.caption: Photograph: Guardian

items: Donald Trump claimed Republicans fared poorly because he was not on the ballot – after repeatedly urging voters to pretend he was on the ballot.
JD Vance pointed to Trump’s ongoing war in Iran as the “obvious” culprit for the loss.

Pete Hegseth’s role leading the unpopular war could lead to him taking the fall – despite Trump publicly backing him. Republicans including Trump foe Thomas Massie have criticized the defense secretary.

Ron DeSantis, Florida’s governor, said the “close to an extinction-level event for Republicans” was caused in part by his party failing to target their ad spending on issues that would motivate voters.

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed Supreme Court Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda as the 28th chief justice of the Supreme Court.
Zalameda, 63, will replace Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who will reach compulsory retirement on November 6.
The appointment was announced by Presidential Communications Office chief Lino Cayetano in a press briefing on Thursday, November 5.
Zalameda will be the first chief justice appointed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., after former President Rodrigo Duterte appointed Gesmundo in 2021.
Marcos chose him after two appointees of former President Benigno Aquino III and two other justices appointed by Duterte.
Duterte appointed him to the Supreme Court on Aug. 6, 2019.
Prior to his Supreme Court stint, he previously served as an associate justice of the Court of Appeals, where he later chaired its 17th Division.

items: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appointed Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda as the 28th Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, replacing Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who is retiring.

Zalameda, who has a history of significant rulings, including acquitting Imelda Marcos of graft charges and defining red-tagging, aims to improve the judiciary by addressing case delays and enhancing technology and employee benefits.

He emphasizes the importance of collegiality among justices and a commitment to the Constitution, while also sharing his background as a public prosecutor and associate justice prior to his Supreme Court appointment.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has chosen Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda as the country’s 28th Supreme Court (SC) chief justice, Malacañang announced on Thursday, November 5.

Zalameda, the third most senior among the chief justice nominees, replaces Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo who will retire on Friday, November 6. Zalameda will serve as chief justice for seven years or until August 2033, when he reaches the mandatory retirement age of 70.
As top magistrate, Zalameda will be the head of the judiciary and all courts in the country. He is tasked to steer the judiciary’s direction, along with the 14 associate justices of the High Court.
For Zalameda’s appointment, Marcos skipped seniority.

He bypassed Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, the second most senior SC justice since May 2022; and Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa. Then-president Benigno Aquino III appointed Leonen in November 2012, and Caguioa in January 2016.
Zalameda authored the SC 1st Division’s ruling that cleared the President’s mother, Imelda Marcos, of seven counts of graft related to Swiss foundations.

The 50-page decision, which had the concurrence of 1st Division members, overturned the Sandiganbayan’s November 2018 decision that convicted the 97-year-old former first lady of seven counts of graft. (READ: Supreme Court acquits Imelda Marcos in 7 counts of graft)

blocks.caption: Not yet justice, but SC ruling gives activists fighting chance vs red-tagging

blocks.text: The new chief justice was also the author of the progressive Deduro v. Vinoya ruling in 2024 that finally defined red-tagging as an act that threatens a person’s right to life, liberty, and security.

Though it was far from justice, activists said the ruling gave them a fighting chance against state attacks because the High Court acknowledged red-tagging as a likely “precursor to abduction or extrajudicial killing,” and being associated communists makes a person a “target of vigilantes, paramilitary groups, or even state agents.”

During his Judicial and Bar Council interviews, Zalameda said his top priorities as chief justice would be building more courthouses to address delays in solving cases, invest in more technology, and improve the benefits of judiciary employees.

“The judiciary must also confront delays that continue to burden litigants. I recognize that not all cases require the same amount of time and effort. We must consider their nature and complexity, the number of parties and witnesses, the volume of evidence, the length of proceedings, and the issues that must be resolved,” said Zalameda.

As then aspiring chief justice, Zalameda said he strongly believes in separation of powers among the branches of the government. He said that he is a follower of the Constitution and of his conscience.
He also said that he will lead with collegiality and respect his fellow members of the bench.

“Collegiality does not mean the absence of disagreement. It means we can disagree without becoming disagreeable, and remain, after the debate and the vote, members of one Court serving one Constitution. This is the kind of collegiality I hope to strengthen — one built on mutual respect, professional trust, and a shared commitment to the institution,” said Zalameda.
Collegiality within the High Court is an important virtue after years of turbulence brought by the ouster of two chief justices: Renato Corona and Maria Lourdes Sereno.
Zalameda, who hails from Caloocan City, was born on August 2, 1963.
After passing the Bar Examinations in 1988, he worked as a branch clerk in Makati City Regional Trial Court. He, after this, ventured into private practice from 1990 to 1995.
In 1995, Zalameda became a public prosecutor. Seven years later, in 2002, he became Mandaluyong’s City Prosecutor.

Before his SC appointment, he worked for 11 years as an associate justice of the Court of Appeals where he chaired the 17th Division. Then-president Rodrigo Duterte appointed him to the High Court on August 6, 2019.

Zalameda, like Gesmundo, earned his law degree from Ateneo de Manila University and was also a member of the Fraternal Order of Utopia. He was an academic scholar and dean’s lister, and served as associate editor of the Ateneo Law Journal and senior staff member of the Ateneo Law Bulletin.
Here is Zalameda’s voting history on some of the biggest cases brought before the SC:

items: Junking of same-sex marriage petition: Concurring; voting was unanimous.
Philippines still obliged to cooperate with the International Criminal Court (ICC): Concurring; voting was unanimous.
Declare Vice President Sara Duterte’s 2025 impeachment complaint unconstitutional: Concurring; voting was unanimous.
Deny Senator Bato dela Rosa’s request for temporary restraining order against his ICC warrant: Concurring.
SC compelling Congress to pass anti-dynasty bill: Concurring.
Return P60-billion PhilHealth funds to national treasury: Concurring. He said that the transfer was unconstitutional, but the government may nonetheless be considered to have acted in good faith.
